subject: math

entries: Two rectangles make one L: split the L into part A, 200 by 120 with area 24 000, and part B, 120 by 140 with area 16 800.
slots.label: Two rectangles make one L
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Trace the edge for the perimeter: walk all six edges - 200, 120, 80, 140, 120 and 260 - and add them to get the perimeter of 920.
slots.label: Trace the edge for the perimeter
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Watch out: the missing corner has no area: the 200 by 260 bounding box gives 52 000, but its corner is empty, so that count is too big.
slots.label: Watch out: the missing corner has no area
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The takeaway: add the areas of the parts for the area, and walk every side for the perimeter.
slots.label: The takeaway
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The amount of surface a shape covers, found for a rectangle by multiplying its length by its width.
slots.label: Area
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The total distance around the edge of a shape: add the lengths of all its sides.
slots.label: Perimeter
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A shape made by joining simpler shapes, like the L made from part A, 200 by 120, and part B, 120 by 140.
slots.label: Composite shape
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The smallest rectangle that a shape fits inside: for this L it is 200 by 260, but part of the box is empty.
slots.label: Bounding box
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: Area and perimeter of an L-shape
